_comment: THE cross-runtime profiling session contract. Go (agent-shim/logging/go/profiling,
imported by the daemon, the store and the sidecar), TypeScript
(agent-shim/logging/ts/profile-session.ts, imported by the shim) and elisp
(profiling.el) each assert their own reading against this file, so every
runtime writes into the one session the collector opened and none of them
can be left profiling.
A SESSION IS ONE DIRECTORY UNDER THE ROOT. The root is root_env when set,
else default_root (~ is the user's home). bin/profile-agent-repl.sh opens a
session by writing its id, one line, into <root>/<active_file>, and closes
it by removing that file. Each runtime RECONCILES on signal (Go and node)
or on a call (Emacs): an active file naming a valid session starts
profiling into <root>/<id>/ (a different session than the running one is
stopped first); no active file stops it. Reconciling is idempotent.
PROFILING IS A WINDOW, NEVER A STANDING SETTING. A runtime stops by itself
max_seconds after it started, and records why, so a collector that died
never leaves a runtime paying for a profile nobody will read.
An active file that names no valid session is a FAILED reconcile, recorded
at error, and starts nothing. sessions lists ids each runtime must judge
the same way.
A RUNTIME THAT CAN BE SIGNALED SAYS SO. Go and node terminate on an
unhandled SIGUSR2, so a runtime that is listening writes
<root>/<armed_dir>/<runtime>-<pid> while it listens and removes it when it
stops; the collector signals only a live pid with that marker, so it never
kills a process from a build that predates profiling.
